stem: $P$ is a point with co-ordinates $({=x}, {=y})$ on a Cartesian plane, and $O$ is the origin. $OP$ forms an angle, $\theta$, measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis. Determine $\text{cosec}\theta$ without using a calculator.
solution: Read off the co-ordinates of $P$ and keep their signs: $x={=x}$ and $y={=y}$. The point lies in quadrant {=q}.

We find $r=OP$ with the theorem of Pythagoras. $r$ is a length, so it is positive in every quadrant: $\begin{aligned}r^{2}&=x^{2}+y^{2}\\&=({=x})^{2}+({=y})^{2}\\&={=r2}\\r&=\sqrt{{=r2}}\end{aligned}$
notes: Standard tier: the book's ex5-7-1c (B(1;-3), cosec) with the point moved to quadrant II, III or IV so the signs matter, and r an unsimplifiable surd (squarefree, never a perfect square). cosec puts r on top, so the key has no rationalising question: sqrt(r2)/y. |y| >= 2 avoids a denominator of 1 or -1. The stem fixes the angle as measured anticlockwise from the positive x-axis (the book's figure shows the reflex angle for B), so the sign of cosec is determined. Instances: 129 distinct points.
